newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market quiet, looks for leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market quiet, looks for leads.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was subdued and quiet by midsession on Wednesday as the trade waited for leads going into the afternoon session, dealers said.
"There was nothing done this morning as the market went back into its stupor. We'll see what kind of lead the Japanese market will give us this afternoon," a trader said.
Dealers said activity in Japan was likewise lacklustre, although the benchmark November contract in Tokyo was up 1.8 yen to 115.1 in the morning session.
Traders reported no fresh buying one day after purchases by China and inquiries from Japan lifted market sentiment.
"I don't think the major consumers were there in the market today although they may come in later," a dealer said.
The market still felt that the prospect of the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) intervening to prop up prices seems unlikely, traders said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 91.50-93.50 U.S. cents a kg from 91.50 cents. September TSR20 was indicated at 136.00 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 135.00 cents.
